changed_in.5.2: Closing a handle that came from `io.popen()` now answers the way `os.execute()` does: three values, describing how the program on the other end ended — `true` or `nil`, then `"exit"` or `"signal"`, then the status or the signal number. Earlier versions answer `true` when the close itself went through, whatever the program made of its work, and `nil` plus a message and a system error code when it did not. Closing an ordinary file handle is unaffected, on either line.
